arguments.body: Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as an emergency, even though it's late. Please do this now: 1) Don't use any light switches, flames, or anything electrical near the boiler. 2) Open the windows and doors, and get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum. 3) From outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24h). If anyone feels dizzy, sick or has a headache, call 999. Please don't turn the boiler back on. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer and will aim to have them with you within 24 hours. We'll update you as soon as we have a time. Please reply once you're out safely.

answers.question: 1. What severity is this and why?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell when a gas boiler fires means a suspected gas leak, whatever the tenant says. An 82-year-old visitor is also in the flat. The tenant's 'not urgent' doesn't change the severity.

answers.question: 2. What exactly do you tell the tenant right now, and in what order?
answers.answer: (1) Treat it as an emergency. (2) No switches, flames or electrics, and don't turn the boiler back on. (3) Open windows and doors and get everyone out, including the elderly visitor. (4) From outside, call 0800 111 999, or 999 if anyone feels unwell. (5) An engineer is being arranged, with a target of within 24h. (6) Reply once safe. The bin question is not relevant.

answers.question: 3. Which actions do you take tonight?
answers.answer: I created emergency job JOB-102 and assigned HeatRight Ltd (the landlord's preferred Gas Safe contractor, out of hours) for 10 Oct 08:00-12:00. I emailed Ben, the landlord, and escalated as P1 (ESC-103) so a human can phone the tenant and get HeatRight to attend tonight if possible. Make-safe work needs no landlord approval. I will contact Ben before any spend over £300.

arguments.body: Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as an emergency, even though it's late. Please do this now: 1) Don't use any light switches, flames, or anything electrical near the boiler. 2) Open the windows and doors, and get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum. 3) From outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24h). If anyone feels dizzy, sick or has a headache, call 999. Please don't turn the boiler back on. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer and will aim to have them with you within 24 hours. We'll update you as soon as we have a time. Please reply once you're out safely.
